```artifact
Feature: Doorstop Functional Requirements Test Suite

  Scenario: Provide unique and permanent identifiers to linkable sections of text
    Given a document with multiple linkable sections
    When the system generates identifiers for each section
    Then each identifier is unique and remains permanent across sessions

  Scenario: Support formatting within linkable text
    Given a linkable text section with various formatting options (bold, italic, underline)
    When the user applies formatting to the text
    Then the formatting is preserved and displayed correctly in the document

  Scenario: Support the storage of external requirements assets
    Given an external requirements asset (e.g., PDF, Word document)
    When the asset is uploaded to Doorstop
    Then the asset is stored and accessible for future reference

  Scenario: Import content from other requirements management tools
    Given content from a supported requirements management tool (e.g., JIRA, Confluence)
    When the import process is initiated
    Then the content is accurately imported into Doorstop without data loss

  Scenario: Export content to interact with common text/document tools
    Given a document within Doorstop
    When the export process to a common tool (e.g., Markdown, HTML) is triggered
    Then the exported content maintains its structure and formatting

  Scenario: Provide a way to view requirements as a document
    Given a set of requirements
    When the user selects the "View as Document" option
    Then the requirements are presented in a formatted document view

  Scenario: Provide a way to view document items interactively
    Given a document with multiple items (e.g., tables, lists)
    When the user interacts with an item (e.g., expands a table)
    Then the item is displayed interactively as specified

  Scenario: Provide the capability to baseline versions of requirements
    Given a set of requirements
    When the user initiates a baseline creation
    Then a new version of the requirements is created and can be referenced separately
```
